GNU uses a different open order (O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK first), so this is a candidate contract; GNU parity of the outcomes is migration-sync-operand-outcomes.

files.inner.sh:
fds() { local f; FDS=; for f in /proc/self/fd/*; do FDS+=" ${f##*/}"; done; }
step() {
  local label=$1; shift
  fds; local before=$FDS
  : <"seg-$label.mark"
  sync "$@" 2>"err-$label.txt"
  printf '%s status=%d\n' "$label" "$?"
  fds; [[ $FDS == "$before" ]] && printf '%s fd-table=unchanged\n' "$label" || printf '%s fd-table=changed\n' "$label"
}
step modes rw.txt ro.txt wo.txt
step failures rw.txt none.txt /dev/null absent.txt ro.txt
: <seg-end.mark
mapfile -t E <err-failures.txt
named=0 stray=0
for line in "${E[@]}"; do
  [[ $line == *none.txt* || $line == *absent.txt* || $line == */dev/null* ]] && ((named++))
  [[ $line == *rw.txt* || $line == *ro.txt* ]] && ((stray++))
done
printf 'failure-diagnostics=%d naming-valid-operands=%d\n' "$named" "$stray"

cases.script:
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/system-seccomp.py
: >"$HOME/calls.jsonl"
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" --notify openat --log-args openat=2 --log-string openat=1 --notify fsync --log-args fsync=0 --notify close --log-args close=0 --log "$HOME/calls.jsonl" -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc inner.sh
printf 'filtered-shell-status=%d\n' "$?"
/usr/bin/python3 syncobs.py segments "$HOME/calls.jsonl" rw.txt ro.txt wo.txt none.txt /dev/null absent.txt
cases.stdout:
modes status=0
modes fd-table=unchanged
failures status=1
failures fd-table=unchanged
failure-diagnostics=3 naming-valid-operands=0
filtered-shell-status=0
== modes
rw.txt open=WRONLY fsync-then-close=same-fd
ro.txt open=WRONLY,RDONLY fsync-then-close=same-fd
wo.txt open=WRONLY fsync-then-close=same-fd
== failures
rw.txt open=WRONLY fsync-then-close=same-fd
none.txt open=WRONLY,RDONLY fsync=none
/dev/null open=WRONLY fsync-then-close=same-fd
absent.txt open=WRONLY,RDONLY fsync=none
ro.txt open=WRONLY,RDONLY fsync-then-close=same-fd
== end
